Content: I personally believe not everything should be saved—it’s just impossible,” Seu notes. To live and thrive online not just as an extremely logged-in individual but also as a society as a whole, the work of digital archiving—in connecting the dots and presenting context and remembering why it’s called the web at all—might be the most radical act of all.  -
“To attempt to preserve all of the past would be life-denying" - Kevin A. Lynch -

The thing is, it’s all more ephemeral than we think, this online-offline world. For example, when I note that she doesn’t appear to own a TV, Seu reveals that she’s kind of against streaming. “I’m a big downloader, because I feel like it’s a way of storing, like a grassroots way of saving what you want to be preserved,” she says. “Owning your content instead of just assuming it’ll be in the cloud forever—it really won’t.” -
